name: X: Open URL
summary: Open one X post, same-author thread or article and return it as one rzn.item/v2.
description: Open one X post URL (/<handle>/status/<id> or /<handle>/article/<id>) read-only and return the post, the author's whole self-thread around it, or the article, as one rzn.item/v2 keyed x:post:<first post id>. Use this to read one post in full. Do not use to list posts (`x_search_posts`, `x_profile_posts`) or to act on a post (`x_like_post`, `x_reply_post`).

url.description: X post URL: /<handle>/status/<id> or /<handle>/article/<id>; any post of a same-author thread returns the whole thread.

steps.name: Keep the post responses the page downloads (TweetResultByRestId, TweetDetail; no request of its own)
Open the post in a fresh tab
Return the post, its self-thread or the article from the captured responses as rzn.item/v2

output_schema.description: rzn.item/v2 (schema/rzn.item.v2.json): one post, self-thread or article, key x:post:<first post id>.

help.summary: Open one X post, same-author thread or article and return it as one rzn.item/v2.

parameters.url: X post URL: /<handle>/status/<id> or /<handle>/article/<id>; any post of a same-author thread returns the whole thread.

examples.description: Read a post and the author's thread under it.

returns: rzn.item/v2 with the X listings' keys: key x:post:<first post id> (a thread's first post, wherever the URL points in it), kind post, url, title (articles), author, published_at (RFC 3339), published_in X, marker edit:<edits>;posts:<n>, fields lang/is_article/in_reply_to, counts likes/reposts/replies/quotes/bookmarks/views of the first post.

Blocks: one post block per post of the self-thread (image/video URLs as attachments) plus a quoted block per quoted post; an article is one block per paragraph (kind paragraph, heading, list_item, quote or code; headings above a block in path).
truncated is set when the thread's first post or an article's body did not load; such an item is not indexed.
notes: Read-only. Never posts, replies, or likes.

Makes no request of its own: a capture_responses step keeps the TweetResultByRestId and TweetDetail responses the post page itself downloads, and the last step maps them (whole text of long posts, exact counts, edit count, thread ids).
